candidates.evidenceBasis: The observation states that nobody on site can determine whether the eyebolt is fixed into the structural deck or is held only in the insulation, and that no identification plate or test/installation record exists for it.
candidates.reasoning: A single-point fall-arrest anchor is about to be used to protect against a fall from a flat roof. Its visible condition (flush collar, undistorted eye, no corrosion) says nothing about what it is actually fixed into beneath the new roof build-up. If it is held only in a 120 mm insulation layer rather than anchored into the structural deck, it will not be capable of arresting a fall, meaning the anchor point itself is a hazard the technician is about to rely on without any means of confirming its load capacity.

evidence.quotedText: clip a fall-arrest lanyard to a single-point eyebolt anchor

candidates.evidenceBasis: The observation states the technician is about to use a single fixed anchor point as the sole fall-arrest attachment for the task.
candidates.reasoning: Reliance on a single anchor point with no secondary or redundant anchorage means that if this one anchor fails or is unsuitable, there is no backup arrest system, and the fall-arrest system as a whole depends entirely on the integrity of the one point currently in question.

clarifications.question: Is the eyebolt anchor fixed through the roof build-up into the structural deck, or is it held only within the insulation layer?
clarifications.whyItMatters: If the anchor is fixed into the structural deck it can plausibly develop the load capacity required to arrest a fall and the task may proceed using it as the fall-arrest point. If it is held only in the insulation layer, it cannot be relied upon to arrest a fall, the technician must not clip to it, and an alternative anchorage or fall-restraint/prevention method must be used instead. The observation states this is unknown on site, and the difference determines whether the planned attachment point may be used at all.
clarifications.evidenceGap: Whether the eyebolt is anchored into the structural deck or only into the insulation layer above it is not known by anyone on site.

explanation.summary: The eyebolt anchor appears visually sound but nobody on site can confirm whether it is fixed into the structural deck or sits only within the new insulation build-up, and there is no identification plate or installation/test record to establish its rated capacity — this is a decision-critical gap because the technician is about to rely on it as the sole fall-arrest point. A secondary concern is that the arrangement uses a single anchor with no redundancy, so the entire fall-arrest system depends on the integrity of this one unverified point. No regulatory record was supplied, so no obligation is asserted; the analysis is limited to what the observation itself establishes.

propertyReview.decisionControllingProperty: Whether the eyebolt anchor is fixed into the structural deck such that it can bear fall-arrest loads
propertyReview.propertyReviewReason: Whether the anchor's fixing point can actually bear fall-arrest loads is the physical/structural condition the safety decision turns on directly; it is not a proxy or test result but the load-bearing state itself. The surface condition of the collar/eye is evidence about corrosion/distortion only, and is correctly distinguished in the fact from the sub-surface fixing property, which remains the controlling condition.
